cards.back: A low-power **IPv6 mesh** protocol on **802.15.4** (same radio as Zigbee), but devices are **natively IP-addressable** (6LoWPAN) — no translating hub. Self-healing mesh; reaches the LAN via a **Thread Border Router**.

An **application-layer** interoperability standard (over IP) giving smart-home devices a **common data model** so they work across **Apple/Google/Amazon/Samsung**. Runs on Thread, Wi-Fi, or Ethernet; local-first, certificate-based.

**Complementary layers**: **Matter = the language** (app layer, what data means); **Thread = a road** (low-power IPv6 mesh transport). A Matter device runs over Thread OR Wi-Fi/Ethernet. (Matter ≈ HTTP of the smart home.)

Constrained devices have little CPU/RAM and tight **energy** budgets (every cycle = battery). Standard crypto (AES) can be too costly/energy-hungry on tiny MCUs. Lightweight crypto = strong security at minimal resource/energy cost.

The **NIST (2023) lightweight cryptography standard** for constrained devices. Provides **AEAD** (authenticated encryption = confidentiality + integrity) **and hashing** in one compact, efficient, side-channel-resistant design.

**ASCON**: small footprint, low energy on tiny MCUs, AEAD by design → built for constrained IoT. **AES**: general-purpose, often hardware-accelerated → great on servers/phones. Same strength; ASCON is a better *fit* for sensors.
**No.** Lightweight = **resource-light** (gates, RAM, energy), NOT security-light. ASCON was chosen via a rigorous multi-year NIST competition for security AND efficiency.

Reducing a device's **visibility/discoverability** so attackers can't easily find/reach it: **gateway/NAT** (no public exposure), **segmentation/VLAN**, **non-standard ports**. A defense-in-depth *layer*.

cards.front: Why does hiding devices behind NAT help?
cards.back: Devices get private, non-routable IPs and only make **outbound** connections, so internet scanners (e.g., **Shodan**) can't reach them — 'you can't attack what you can't see.' The gateway is shield + translator.
**Security through obscurity**: cuts opportunistic/automated default-port scanning, but a determined attacker scans all ports. **Never** a substitute for authentication + encryption.

The **outer fence, not the vault door** — one layer of defense-in-depth. Stack it: hide (obfuscation) → authenticate → encrypt (ASCON) → verify every request (Zero Trust). Each layer assumes the prior may fail.
